record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Does there exist an asymptotically flat metric on R3 with zero scalar curvature that admits a minimal 2-sphere, and can such a minimal 2-sphere be stable; alternatively, can one prove that no such metric exists?

evidence.quote: Find an AF metric on R3 with zero scalar curvature and admitting a minimal 2-sphere, or prove there is no such metric. This is the previous question, but requiring a time-symmetric initial data set. Can the 2-sphere be a stable minimal surface?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A complete Riemannian metric $g$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ is called asymptotically flat if there exists a compact set $K \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ and a diffeomorphism from $\mathbb{R}^3 \setminus K$ to the complement of a ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$ such that, in the induced coordinates $(x^1,x^2,x^3)$, the metric components satisfy
$$g_{ij}(x) = \delta_{ij} + O(|x|^{-1}), \qquad \partial_k g_{ij}(x) = O(|x|^{-2}), \qquad \partial_k\partial_l g_{ij}(x) = O(|x|^{-3})$$
as $|x| \to \infty$, and the scalar curvature is integrable. The metric is said to be scalar-flat if its scalar curvature satisfies $R_g \equiv 0$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$. A closed embedded 2-sphere $\Sigma \subset (\mathbb{R}^3, g)$ is minimal if its mean curvature vanishes identically, and is stable if the second variation of area is non-negative for all smooth normal variations.

Decide which of the following holds:
(a) There exists an asymptotically flat, scalar-flat metric $g$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ that admits a minimal embedded 2-sphere; moreover, such a minimal 2-sphere can be chosen to be stable.
(b) No asymptotically flat, scalar-flat metric on $\mathbb{R}^3$ admits a minimal embedded 2-sphere.

Either construct such a metric (with a stable minimal 2-sphere if possible) or prove that no such metric exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The existence question has been answered affirmatively. Constructions by P. Miao and by Chruściel–Delay produce asymptotically flat, scalar-flat metrics on $\mathbb{R}^3$ admitting (multiple) stable minimal 2-spheres; in particular, time-symmetric vacuum initial data containing apparent horizons (stable minimal spheres) provide such examples.

status_evidence.title: A note on asymptotically flat metrics on R^3 which are scalar-flat and admit minimal spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions by Miao and Chruściel-Delay can be used to produce asymptotically flat metrics on R^3 which have zero scalar curvature and multiple stable minimal spheres.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit constructions yield asymptotically flat scalar-flat metrics on R^3 with stable minimal 2-spheres.

status_evidence.title: A note on asymptotically flat metrics on R^3 which are scalar-flat and admit minimal spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Such metrics are solutions of the time-symmetric vacuum constraint equations of general relativity; horizons of black holes are stable minimal spheres.
status_evidence.claim: Affirmative resolution: stable minimal spheres can occur in scalar-flat AF metrics on R^3.
